clue.text: Paul wasn't sighted entering this capital

definitions.text: Paul wasn't sighted entering this capital

parts.words: Paul wasn't sighted entering this capital
parts.note: Saul, later the apostle Paul, was struck blind on the road and led sightless into the Syrian city

explanation.surface: A remark about a man called Paul who could not see as he arrived in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Syrian capital is the city Saul was led into blind after his conversion vision.

clue.text: Move from office to testify

definitions.meaning: to remove a ruler or official from power
to give sworn evidence, as a deponent does

explanation.surface: An official is removed from post and then called to give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting a ruler and making a sworn statement in law are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: Streaked like Tom? Reckoned without false alarm

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: reckoned, as in made it ten, means made

indicators.note: a false version of the word alarm is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: Someone works out that a tomcat's streaks were no cause for a false alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: MADE goes around RMALA, the anagram of ALARM signalled by 'false'. 'Tom' is a tomcat, so the definition is a ginger tabby's colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger tabby tomcat with orange stripes is called a marmalade cat.

clue.text: Virtuous tinker is not commonly put inside

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, as a prisoner is put inside

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: A virtuous travelling mender is, unusually, not sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Sly the tinker is a literary allusion to the opening of The Taming of the Shrew; 'put inside' places AINT in SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone virtuous lives like a holy person, upright and good.

clue.text: Demoralize an internationalist

definitions.meaning: to take away someone's courage or nerve
read as two words, a man working for the United Nations

explanation.surface: An internationalist sets out to dishearten someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve is to sap someone's courage; split in two it is a United Nations man.

clue.text: Engagement pursued by suitor

definitions.meaning: a military engagement is a fight or battle
a suitor here is someone bringing a lawsuit, who pursues a case in court

explanation.surface: A romantic engagement is chased by a hopeful admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is military combat, and a lawsuit is a legal proceeding a litigant brings.

clue.text: Such an uproar in the States sounds like a bad mistake

definitions.text: Such an uproar in the States

indicators.note: signals that the answer is said the same as the word for a blunder

parts.note: a clanger is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: An American commotion is likened to a terrible blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: CLANGER is British slang for a howler; CLANGOR is the American spelling of clangour.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing din, spelt without the u in American English.

clue.text: Like this in Arctic ie rawer

definitions.text: Like this in Arctic ie rawer

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something in the Arctic is described as being colder and more raw.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'arctIC IE Rawer'; the whole clue describes the polar weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar conditions are colder and more frosty, as the clue's description says.

clue.text: Absurdity no three-quarters must repeat

indicators.note: the compass letters are given twice over

parts.note: three of the four compass quarters: north, south and east

explanation.surface: Something silly is said to be three-quarters gone and bound to recur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters' is not a fraction but three compass points, N, S and E; 'must repeat' doubles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurdity is foolish talk or behaviour, rubbish.

clue.text: Musicians in concert in full costume

definitions.meaning: a group of players performing together
a complete matching outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Players at a concert appear in full costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of performers, or a coordinated outfit worn together, both share the French word.

clue.text: One of His Majesty's Opposition?

parts.note: the official opposition party sits in the House of Commons, so any of its members is an MP

explanation.surface: A question about who belongs to the opposition party at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: His Majesty's Opposition is the official name of the main opposition party in the UK Parliament; the clue is fair because every member sits in the House.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a legislature, such as the House of Commons, is called this.

clue.text: Speed up return of Tyneside transport

indicators.note: return means both pieces are read in the backwards direction

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
trams are a form of urban transport

explanation.surface: A call to make the trams on Tyneside go back and forth more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns NETRAMS backwards. Tyneside is the Newcastle area in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something smart, in the sense of brisk, is to quicken it.

clue.text: As grenade explodes, defend yourself!

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the letters of the word grenade

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a warning to guard yourself as a bomb goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's call to take guard, warning an opponent to be ready.

clue.text: Inseparable pair in nursery rhyme writer related to Charles

definitions.meaning: the girl and the pet that followed her to school in the rhyme
the sister of essayist Charles Lamb, co-author of Tales from Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme duo is linked to a writer named Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's girl and her woolly pet, or the essayist's sister who wrote with him.

clue.text: Caution ordered, so man hid

indicators.note: the letters of so man hid are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning is issued, so a man goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution is to warn or reprove someone.

clue.text: They include painters familiar to experts

definitions.meaning: a painter is a line used to tie up a small boat
experts are said to know these, meaning the routine

explanation.surface: A group described as including artists who are well known to specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Cords include a boat's mooring line, and the idiom says experts know them.

clue.text: Well-known beetle

definitions.meaning: famous or eminent
as an adjective, beetle means overhanging or jutting, as in beetle brows

explanation.surface: A famous insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent people are famous, and a beetle brow is one that juts out.

clue.text: Brushed off, and put on more polish

definitions.meaning: snubbed or turned away
buffed a second time

explanation.surface: Someone shines shoes again after being brushed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Snubbed means rejected curtly; buffed again means polished once more.

clue.text: Vessels that may appear after six. for TV audience

indicators.note: these vessels follow the six to make the audience, so they are what remains once it is taken away

parts.note: people watching television are viewers
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Containers that turn up after six o'clock for television watchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that may appear after' means VI followed by the answer makes VIEWERS; the full stop after 'six' is a print slip for a comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugs or pitchers are containers for liquid.

clue.text: Thus shutting up drink with navy in port

indicators.note: the first word encloses the others like a box shut on them

parts.note: so means thus
ale is a drink
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to stop drinking with the navy while in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shutting up' puts ALE and RN inside SO. SALERNO is a port in southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian seaport on the Tyrrhenian coast.

clue.text: Top musicians wrecked in sea storm

indicators.note: a wrecked sea storm has its letters broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Leading players are shipwrecked in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Great conductors or virtuosi are masters of their art.

clue.text: Guy's attached to this little drink of wine

indicators.note: of puts the small measure before the wine in the clue, though the wine comes first

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine
a peg is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A man is fond of a small glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope, which is tied to this. TENT is an archaic word for red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope from a tent is fastened to a stake driven into the ground.

clue.text: One female bird or another catching a male

indicators.note: the first piece catches the others, holding them inside

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
he refers to a male

explanation.surface: A female bird of one kind or another seizes a male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts A and HE inside PEN; 'another' defines a second female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The female peafowl is a different female bird from the swan.

clue.text: One corresponding to you, say, among foreign letters

definitions.text: One corresponding to you, say, among foreign letters

parts.words: One corresponding to you, say, among foreign letters
parts.note: the Greek alphabet has a character for the sound of the English letter u, which sounds like you

explanation.surface: Someone who writes to you is described as one of your foreign correspondents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corresponding to you' suggests a pen pal, but it means matching the letter u, said like 'you', in the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet matches the Roman u.

clue.text: Aim makes sense

definitions.meaning: the part of a gun used to aim it
vision, one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Aiming is said to be sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's aiming device and the faculty of vision share the word.

clue.text: Insures variety star's regular appearance

indicators.note: a variety of the word insures is the same letters in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A variety show insures its star who appears regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges INSURES; the star is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is when the sun, a star, comes up every day.

clue.text: Seat associated with centre of party hitherto

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A seat linked to the middle of a political party so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes R, the middle letter of 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means until now, up to this point.

clue.text: Spokesman's statistics? Don't take them literally

definitions.meaning: a spokesman deals in speech, so his numbers would be its figures
metaphors and similes are expressions not meant literally

explanation.surface: A press officer's numbers should not be taken at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphors and idioms are non-literal expressions; figures of a spokesman's speech would be his statistics.

clue.text: How rifle may be carried back, as not required

indicators.note: back means the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: a rifle at the port is ported, held diagonally across the body

explanation.surface: A soldier is told how to carry a rifle on the back, as it is no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PORTED round. A rifle held at port arms is said to be ported.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing meaning superfluous or unwanted.

clue.text: Provide illuminations for resort, say

indicators.note: say tells us the answer is spoken like the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside town is asked to put on its annual light display.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside town on England's south coast; 'say' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten or make lighter is to illuminate.
